verses.10:2: No Senhor confio: † {quomodo} à minha alma: * {transmigra} {passer}?
verses.10:3: Porque eis que os pecadores {arcum}, † prepararam as suas setas na aljava, * para {sagittent} no escuro os retos de coração.
verses.10:5a: O Senhor está no seu templo santo, * {sedes}.
verses.10:5b: Os seus olhos {respiciunt} o pobre: * as suas pálpebras {interrogant} os filhos dos homens.
verses.10:6: O Senhor {interrogat} o justo e o ímpio: * mas quem ama a iniquidade odeia {animam}.
verses.10:7: {pluet} sobre os pecadores: * fogo e enxofre e {procellarum} {calicis}.
verses.10:8: Porque o Senhor é justo, e amou {justitias}: * {vidit}.

decisions.why: quómodo is ‘how’ (πῶς): the question of one who cannot see how the advice can be given to a man who trusts in the Lord. Douay-Rheims ‘how then do you say’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘porque dizeis (pois)’ reads it as ‘why’. The speakers are plural (dícitis), so vós. Heard (draft 1): the blind reader took ‘como dizeis à minha alma’ first as a question put to the Lord, ‘mencionado imediatamente antes’ — a cost of vós: in the Latin the number tells the two addressees apart (dícitis, plural, the advisers; perfecísti, 10:4, singular, God), in Portuguese both are ‘vós’.

options.label: como dizeis vós
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the subject hidden in the verb ending is named (D2 allows it), and set straight against ‘o Senhor’ of the first colon — in the Lord I trust; how can you say … — so that the hearer is told that ‘vós’ here is someone other than the Lord. Nothing is added that the Latin’s ‘dícitis’ does not say. One syllable more; the colon is still shorter than the Latin’s.

options.label: como dizeis
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s ‘how’ (Douay-Rheims). Heard by the blind reader first as said to the Lord.

options.label: por que dizeis
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Asks for a reason, where the Latin asks how it can be said at all.

decisions.why: transmígrare: ‘to remove from one place to another, to migrate’ (Lewis & Short; the verb is only here in the psalter, grep). The Greek μεταναστεύου is ‘change your dwelling’. The advice is to move house to the mountain; it does not say ‘flee’. Douay-Rheims ‘Get thee away from hence to the mountain’; Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal (from the Hebrew) ‘Foge’. The soul is addressed alone, so tu.

options.label: Muda-te para o monte
options.note: Ruling: ‘mudar-se’ is exactly to change one’s dwelling, the plain verb of the Greek and of Lewis & Short’s first sense. It keeps the advice as advice, not panic.

options.label: Migra para o monte
options.note: Keeps the Latin’s root, and ‘migrar’ is what birds do, which prepares the sparrow. The tu imperative ‘migra’ is rarely said.

options.label: Passa para o monte
options.note: The ‘trans-’ heard; weaker as a change of home.

options.label: Foge para o monte
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (and the Diurnal, from the Hebrew). Refused: flight is an interpretation; the Latin says remove, migrate (D2).

decisions.why: passer is the sparrow (στρουθίον); five verses (grep: 10:2, 83:4, 101:8 sicut passer solitárius in tecto, 103:16 pásseres, 123:7a Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est de láqueo). Douay-Rheims ‘sparrow’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘a ave’. Rule 5: concrete images stay concrete.

options.label: como um pardal
options.note: Ruling, proposed for the glossary (passer → pardal): the named bird, the plain Brazilian word; it serves all five places (‘como um pardal solitário no telhado’, ‘a nossa alma, como um pardal, foi arrancada do laço’). The indefinite article, as Portuguese says a simile.

options.label: como a ave
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Generic where the Latin names a small, defenceless bird.

options.label: como um passarinho
options.note: The small bird without the species; tender, and a diminutive the Latin does not have.

decisions.why: Glossary: téndere / inténdere arcum → armar o arco (open; Ps 7:13 ‘armou o seu arco’), which names 10:3 among the places where inténdere cannot be ‘atender’ (D3). 63:4 has the same phrase and the same purpose clause (intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum) and will copy this verse. The Latin has no possessive with arcum (it has one with sagíttas).

options.label: armaram o arco
options.note: Ruling: the glossary’s wording, without a possessive the Latin does not have. Douay-Rheims ‘have bent their bow’.

options.label: retesaram o arco
options.note: The exact verb (to draw the string taut); the glossary names it as little known.

options.label: estenderam o seu arco
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. ‘Estender um arco’ is not said of a bow in Portuguese, and the possessive is supplied.

decisions.latin: ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde
decisions.why: sagittáre: ‘to discharge arrows, to shoot with arrows’ (Lewis & Short, citing this verse and 63:4). The Latin makes a figure of sagíttas … sagíttent; the Greek has βέλη … κατατοξεῦσαι, no echo. Douay-Rheims ‘to shoot in the dark the upright of heart’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘para as dispararem na obscuridade contra os que são de coração recto’. rectus corde → reto de coração (glossary, Ps 7:11). in obscúro → ‘no escuro’ (the Greek is ‘in a moonless night’).

options.label: flecharem
options.note: Ruling: the plain Brazilian verb for shooting a person with arrows, transitive as the Latin is, so ‘os retos de coração’ stays the direct object. Cost: seta (glossary for sagítta) and flechar are two roots, so the Latin’s echo sagíttas / sagíttent is not heard.

options.label: assetearem
options.note: Keeps the echo (setas … assetearem) exactly; ‘assetear’ is in the dictionary but hardly said in Brazil — rule 5 (no word needing a footnote).

options.label: dispararem contra
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. The arrows are left implicit and a preposition supplied.

decisions.why: perfícere → aperfeiçoar (glossary, open, from Ps 8:3; the row says it was tried on this verse). The Greek κατηρτίσω is ‘you fitted, established’ — the Hebrew has ‘the foundations’, another reading. Douay-Rheims ‘they have destroyed the things which thou hast made’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘destruíram o que fizeste de bom’. The Latin puts the object first; destrúere → destruir (glossary; not at the vós imperative, so safe here).

options.label: destruíram o que aperfeiçoastes
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb, in natural Portuguese order (D2); the subject is the sinners of 10:3. The colon ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: o que aperfeiçoastes, eles destruíram
options.note: The Latin’s order, with the object first and a subject named; the glossary’s trial wording. Heavier.

options.label: destruíram o que levastes à perfeição

forms.perfecisti: destruíram o que levastes à perfeição

options.note: Avoids the everyday sense of ‘aperfeiçoar’ (to improve what was wanting); three syllables longer.

options.label: destruíram o que fizestes de bom

forms.perfecisti: destruíram o que fizestes de bom

options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Refused: ‘de bom’ is his gloss and ‘fizestes’ is fácere’s verb (Douay-Rheims ‘made’ has the same flattening).

decisions.why: A perfect: ‘but the just man, what has he done?’ — open between ‘what wrong did he do to deserve this?’ (Matos Soares 1932’s gloss ‘de mau’) and ‘what has he achieved / can he do?’ (the Hebrew’s ‘what can the righteous do?’, which the Diurnal follows). Douay-Rheims ‘but what has the just man done?’.

options.label: mas que fez o justo
options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s tense and its openness; natural order, and the verse ends on the just man, as the Latin’s question ends on his deed. No gloss. Heard: the blind reader took it first as ‘que mal o justo fez para merecer isso?’, second as ‘what did he do in the face of the destruction’ — both are in the Latin.

options.label: mas o justo, que fez
options.note: The Latin’s order (justus autem quid fecit), the just man put first; the verse then closes on an oxytone.

options.label: mas que pode fazer o justo

forms.justus: mas que pode fazer o justo

options.note: The Hebrew’s sense, as the Diurnal has it. Refused: the Latin has a perfect (D2).

decisions.why: Both colons of 10:5a are verbless and both begin ‘Dóminus’; the second is a hanging nominative: ‘the Lord — in heaven is his seat’. Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 dissolve it into ‘the Lord’s throne is in heaven’, which loses the anaphora. sedes → ‘trono’ (the Greek θρόνος; Portuguese ‘sede’ is headquarters or thirst, ‘assento’ is a chair).

options.label: o Senhor tem no céu o seu trono

forms.sedes: o Senhor tem no céu o seu trono

options.note: Ruling: the anaphora kept (O Senhor … o Senhor), the Latin’s possessive ‘ejus’ turned into the verb Portuguese uses for it; a verb supplied as the first colon supplies ‘está’ (D2). Ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: o Senhor, no céu está o seu trono

forms.sedes: o Senhor, no céu está o seu trono

options.note: The Latin’s hanging nominative kept. Correct in speech, loose on the page.

options.label: o trono do Senhor está no céu

forms.sedes: o trono do Senhor está no céu

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and Douay-Rheims. Refused: the repetition ‘Dóminus … Dóminus’ at the head of both colons is the Latin’s (D2).

decisions.why: respícere in: to look (back) at, to regard (the Greek ἀποβλέπουσιν, to look away towards, fix one’s gaze on). The imperative returns in 12:3 (réspice, ἐπίβλεψον — the verb of 118:132 Áspice in me → ‘Olhai para mim’). Douay-Rheims ‘look on the poor man’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘olham para o pobre’. pauper → ‘pobre’ (the plain word; 11:6a sets it beside inops). The stylist (draft 1): ‘«olhos olham» repete sons muito próximos e faz a boca tropeçar; essa repetição não corresponde a uma repetição de raiz no latim’ → ‘Os seus olhos estão voltados para o pobre’.

options.label: estão voltados para
options.note: Ruling (draft 2), the stylist’s: the jingle gone, and the re- of respícere (to look back, turn one’s gaze to) heard. It is a participle of state (‘facing, turned towards’), not the reflexive ‘voltar-se’ that is convértere’s verb (glossary; Ps 5:8b has the same ‘voltado para’ for ad). Cost: a present of action becomes a state — to be weighed by the gate.

options.label: olham para
options.note: Draft 1: Matos Soares 1932’s words. Refused by the stylist for the jingle ‘olhos olham’, which the Latin does not have (Ps 53:9 accepted ‘o meu olho olhou’, where the Latin has óculus … despéxit).

options.label: se voltam para
options.note: The re- of respícere heard, and no jingle; ‘voltar-se’ is convértere’s verb (6:5 Voltai-vos).

options.label: contemplam
options.note: Warm and sayable; the verb of contemplári / consideráre (90:8 considerábis → contemplarás).

decisions.why: One verb twice in consecutive verses (the Greek too: ἐξετάζει twice), so one Portuguese verb (rule 6). interrogáre: ‘to ask, question’, in particular ‘to interrogate judicially, to examine’ (Lewis & Short) — the judge questioning the parties, which is the scene of 10:5–6. Douay-Rheims ‘examine … trieth’ (two words for one); Matos Soares 1932 ‘examinam … sonda’. Other places: 34:11, 136:3a, 138:23 intérroga me (grep).

options.label: interrogam … interroga
options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s word, and its image — eyelids that question — kept whole (rule 5); Portuguese ‘interrogar’ has the judicial sense too. The same verb both times. Heard: in 10:6 the blind reader took ‘interroga’ first as ‘faz perguntas ou exige explicações’, second as ‘examina ou põe à prova’ — the Latin verb’s own two senses; in 10:5b the eyelids were heard as a look that examines. The Latinist passed it.

options.label: examinam … examina
options.note: The Greek’s sense and Douay-Rheims’ first word; plainer, and the scrutiny of the eyelids is easier to picture. Loses the question.

options.label: sondam … sonda
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 in 10:6 (and the Diurnal). Refused: ‘sondar’ is scrutári’s (glossary; 7:10).

decisions.why: suam is reflexive (the Greek τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν): he hates his own soul, i.e. himself. Douay-Rheims ‘hateth his own soul’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘odeia a sua alma’. ánima → alma (glossary), with the known cost that ánima can be ‘life’.

options.label: a sua alma
options.note: Ruling: Matos Soares 1932; ‘sua’ after the subject ‘quem ama’ is heard as his own, and God is ‘vós’ throughout, so ‘sua’ cannot be taken as God’s.

options.label: a sua própria alma
options.note: Douay-Rheims ‘his own’: the reflexive marked, two syllables more.

options.label: a sua vida
options.note: The other sense of ánima; decides what the Latin leaves open.

decisions.why: plúere used transitively, ‘he will rain snares’ (the Greek ἐπιβρέξει likewise); the subject is the Lord of 10:6. láqueus → laço (glossary). Douay-Rheims ‘He shall rain snares upon sinners’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘Fará chover laços … sobre os pecadores’. The same verb in 77:24, 77:27 (pluit illis manna).

options.label: Fará chover laços
options.note: Ruling: Matos Soares 1932 — the Portuguese idiom for a transitive ‘rain’; grammar, not sense (D2).

options.label: Choverá laços
options.note: One verb for one; transitive ‘chover’ is heard as impersonal (‘it will rain snares’), which loses the Lord as subject.

decisions.why: spíritus here is wind, breath (the Greek πνεῦμα καταιγίδος, ‘wind of the tempest’); procella a violent storm. The phrase returns in 148:8 (Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum), which should match. Douay-Rheims ‘storms of winds’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘as tempestades’ (spíritus dropped). ‘Espírito’ in Portuguese is never wind.

options.label: vento de tempestades
options.note: Ruling: bare nouns, as the Latin list is bare (fogo, e enxofre, e vento de tempestades), and the plural kept. Proposed for 148:8 too.

options.label: o sopro das tempestades
options.note: ‘Sopro’ keeps spíritus as breath; with the article it breaks the run of bare nouns.

options.label: tempestades
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Drops spíritus.

decisions.why: The second colon of 10:7 has no verb. pars → parte (glossary keeps porção for pórtio); calix → cálice (15:5 pars hereditátis meæ et cálicis mei, 22:5, 74:8, 115:4). Douay-Rheims supplies ‘shall be the portion of their cup’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘são a parte que lhes toca’ (the cup dropped). ‘Cálice’ is a proparoxytone and cannot close the verse (rule 4), so ‘eórum’ becomes ‘deles’, which also keeps ‘seu’ from being heard as God’s.

options.label: são a parte do cálice deles

forms.calicis: são a parte do cálice deles

options.note: Ruling: a present copula supplied, as the Latin’s nominal sentence reads (Matos Soares 1932); the cup kept; the verse ends on a paroxytone. Heard: the blind reader understood ‘a porção de sofrimento ou castigo que lhes cabe’, the cup’s old sense.

options.label: serão a parte do cálice deles

forms.calicis: serão a parte do cálice deles

options.note: Douay-Rheims’ tense, following ‘Pluet’. The Latin states it without a verb, as a standing fact.

options.label: são a porção do seu cálice

forms.calicis: são a porção do seu cálice

options.note: ‘Porção’ is pórtio’s (glossary), and the verse would end on a proparoxytone.

options.label: são a parte que lhes toca

forms.calicis: são a parte que lhes toca

options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Refused: the cup is the Latin’s image (rule 5).

decisions.why: justítias is plural, as the Greek δικαιοσύνας: just deeds, the acts of justice. Douay-Rheims ‘hath loved justice’ and Matos Soares 1932 ‘ama a justiça’ both make it singular (Matos Soares also present). The plural returns in 17:23, 49:16, 74:3, 88:32, 147:8 (grep) — in several of them it stands for another Greek word (δικαιώματα), so they decide locally. diléxit is a perfect: ‘amou’.

options.label: as justiças
options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s number kept — the plural of an abstract noun names its deeds, as ‘as misericórdias’ does. Tested: the blind reader heard ‘os atos ou comportamentos justos’ first, not the courts; the Latinist passed it.

options.label: a justiça
options.note: Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932. The number is lost.

options.label: as obras de justiça
options.note: Says what the plural means; a noun supplied (explains).

decisions.why: The Latin says that his face saw equity (the Greek εὐθύτητα εἶδεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ); the Hebrew reads the other way (the upright shall behold his face), which the Diurnal follows. Object first in the Latin; in Portuguese the object cannot go first without being heard as the subject. vultus → rosto (Ps 4:7 ‘a luz do vosso rosto’); ǽquitas → equidade (glossary). Douay-Rheims ‘his countenance hath beheld righteousness’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘o seu rosto olha para a equidade’.

options.label: o seu rosto viu a equidade

forms.vidit: o seu rosto viu a equidade

options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s verb and tense, in the only order that keeps the roles; ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: o seu rosto olha para a equidade

forms.vidit: o seu rosto olha para a equidade

options.note: Matos Soares 1932. A present, and ‘olhar para’ is respícere’s verb one verse before.

options.label: a sua face viu a equidade

forms.vidit: a sua face viu a equidade

options.note: ‘Face’ is fácies’s word (glossary); vultus is ‘rosto’.

options.label: os retos verão a sua face

forms.vidit: os retos verão a sua face

options.note: The Hebrew’s sense (the Diurnal: ‘contemplarão sua face os homens retos’). Refused: it is not the Latin (rule 1).

choices.10:2: The psalm begins at 10:2 (10:1 is the titulus; D7). In Dómino confído → ‘No Senhor confio’: confídere in → confiar em (glossary), in the Latin’s order, which is also natural Portuguese (Matos Soares 1932 has the same words). The first colon is the psalm’s confession; the rest of the verse is the advice of others (plural: dizeis), addressed to the soul (singular: tu). Heard: the blind reader took ‘dizeis’ first as said to the Lord — a cost of vós (decision quomodo); draft 2 names the subject.
choices.10:3: ‘Porque eis que’ for Quóniam ecce: quóniam → porque (as 8:2b, 8:4), ecce → eis (glossary). sagítta → seta (glossary); pháretra → ‘aljava’, only here in the psalter (grep) — the one word for a quiver. 63:4 has the same frame (intendérunt arcum … ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum) and should copy the wording of this verse. The blind reader listed ‘aljava’ as unknown; there is no plainer word for a quiver, and the image is the Latin’s; kept.
choices.10:5a: ‘templo santo’ as in Ps 5:8b (‘o vosso templo santo’); 17:7b has ‘de templo sancto suo’ too. The first colon supplies ‘está’ (D2).
choices.10:5b: pálpebræ → ‘pálpebras’: the concrete image kept (rule 5); the only other place is 131:4. fílii hóminum → ‘filhos dos homens’ (glossary). The mediant word ‘pobre’ is a paroxytone.
choices.10:6: qui autem → ‘mas quem’; dilígere → amar, odísse → odiar (glossary). iníquitas → iniquidade.
choices.10:7: The list keeps the Latin’s repeated ‘et’ (fogo e enxofre e …): rule 2. Draft 1 had commas before each ‘e’ (fogo, e enxofre, e …); the stylist heard them as small stops that break a colon already long, and the two ‘e’ carry the weight — taken (punctuation only). The second colon is the psalm’s heaviest (+4 on the Latin’s 20 syllables), as it is in the Latin.
choices.10:8: justus Dóminus → ‘o Senhor é justo’ (copula supplied; D2). Heard: ‘as justiças’ was understood first as ‘os atos justos’ — the test the decision asked for; the plural stands. ‘o seu rosto’ was heard as the Lord’s.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm10.txt, eight prayed verses with DO’s ids (10:2–10:4, 10:5a, 10:5b, 10:6–10:8). 10:2 and 10:3 have a flex and a mediant; every other verse one ‘*’. 10:1 is the titulus (D7). Douay-Rheims is not in Bolls for this psalm: it was fetched from drbo.org by the first agent (ps010/drb.txt; consult/drbo-ps010.htm), and parallels.py now reads it.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps010.md. Sense from the Vulgate family (Douay-Rheims from drbo.org; Matos Soares 1932 by its text layer). The Diurnal Monástico 1962 has the psalm, made from the Hebrew: it lends no sense — refused wherever it follows the Hebrew against the Latin (10:4 the foundations / what can the just do; 10:8 the upright shall see his face; 10:7 coals). DO’s Portuguese not used (D12). Lewis & Short read for transmigro, interrogo, sagitto. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: 63:4 intendérunt arcum … ut sagíttent (the twin of 10:3b); 148:8 spíritus procellárum; passer 83:4, 101:8, 103:16, 123:7a; pálpebræ 131:4; interrogáre 34:11, 136:3a, 138:23; justítias (plural) 17:23, 49:16, 74:3, 88:32, 147:8; templo sancto suo 17:7b; confído 24:1. No vós imperative in the psalm (the one imperative, Tránsmigra, is said to the soul: tu). Septuagintal readings kept against the Hebrew: 10:3 in obscúro; 10:4 quæ perfecísti; 10:6 Dóminus intérrogat justum et ímpium; 10:7 láqueos; 10:8 æquitátem vidit vultus ejus. Glossary applied: confiar em, seta, armar o arco, retos de coração, aperfeiçoar, destruir, templo santo, filhos dos homens, amar / odiar, laço, equidade, rosto.

Draft 1: hard pass (ids and marks). Soft flags, all accepted: 10:2 third colon +3 (‘Muda-te para o monte como um pardal’: the article of the simile and ‘para’); 10:3 last colon +4 (‘os retos de coração’ is the glossary’s length for rectos corde); 10:7 second colon +4 (a copula supplied, ‘deles’ for eórum so that the verse does not end on the proparoxytone ‘cálice’). Every cadence is oxytone or paroxytone.

Draft 1: clean — ‘A tradução conserva o sentido do latim em todos os versículos, incluindo suas imagens concretas, tempos verbais e peculiaridades septuagintais. As marcas de divisão são as mesmas e aparecem na mesma ordem que no latim.’ Passed without remark: ‘Muda-te’, ‘pardal’, ‘flecharem’, ‘aperfeiçoastes’ in natural order, ‘o Senhor tem no céu o seu trono’, ‘interrogam … interroga’, ‘as justiças’, ‘o seu rosto viu a equidade’.

Draft 1. Two verses, both ‘sayable’; best 10:4, worst 10:7. ‘O salmo soa sóbrio e reverente, com terminações adequadas ao canto e sem rimas insistentes nas cadências. As imagens incomuns permanecem concretas.’ Both taken: they change only how the thing is said (D2).

outcomes.remark: ‘olhos olham’ makes the mouth stumble, a repetition the Latin does not have → ‘Os seus olhos estão voltados para o pobre’
outcomes.reason: The jingle is not the Latin’s; ‘estar voltado para’ also lets the re- of respícere be heard. ‘Olham para’ stays option 2.

outcomes.remark: the commas of ‘fogo, e enxofre, e vento de tempestades’ fragment an already long colon → ‘fogo e enxofre e vento de tempestades’
outcomes.reason: Punctuation only; the Latin’s repeated ‘et’ is kept.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. Seventeen items, four unknown words (aljava, ímpio, iniquidade, equidade). One real fault: 10:2 ‘como dizeis à minha alma’ heard first as said to the Lord — a cost of vós, mended in draft 2. Everything else is the Latin’s own range, and the plural ‘as justiças’ (10:8), which the draft had put to the test, was heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘como dizeis’: said to other people / to the Lord (heard first)
outcomes.reason: A fault the Latin does not have (dícitis is plural, God is singular in 10:4); draft 2 names the subject, ‘como dizeis vós’, against ‘o Senhor’ of the first colon.

outcomes.remark: ‘à minha alma’: to me / to the spiritual part of me
outcomes.reason: ánima → alma (glossary); the Latin is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘no escuro’: in darkness / in secret
outcomes.reason: in obscúro holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘destruíram’: the sinners / others
outcomes.reason: The sinners were heard first; the Latin leaves the subject in the verb as well.

outcomes.remark: ‘o que aperfeiçoastes’: the Lord’s work (heard first) / the addressees’ of 10:2
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; the naming of ‘vós’ in 10:2 (draft 2) should make the turn to God plainer still.

outcomes.remark: ‘mas que fez o justo?’: what did he do in the face of it / what wrong did he do (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Both are in the Latin’s perfect.

outcomes.remark: ‘as suas pálpebras’: the Lord’s (heard first) / the poor man’s
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; ejus … ejus in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: ‘as suas pálpebras interrogam’: the gaze examines / the eyelids ask questions
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s image; ‘examinam’ is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘os filhos dos homens’: mankind (heard first) / sons of certain men
outcomes.reason: Glossary; heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘interroga’: asks questions, demands explanations (heard first) / examines, tests
outcomes.reason: Both are senses of interrogáre (Lewis & Short: to question; to examine judicially).

outcomes.remark: ‘odeia a sua alma’: his own (heard first) / another’s
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; ‘a sua própria alma’ is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘a sua alma’: the spiritual part (heard first) / the person, his life
outcomes.reason: ánima is as open (glossary: a minha alma, with vida as the known alternative).

outcomes.remark: ‘Fará chover’: the Lord (heard first) / the lover of iniquity
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; the Latin leaves the subject in the verb.

outcomes.remark: ‘laços’: snares (heard first) / ribbons
outcomes.reason: láqueus → laço (glossary, Ps 90:3); heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘a parte do cálice deles’: the punishment that falls to them (heard first) / part of a cup
outcomes.reason: The cup’s figurative sense was heard; the image is the Latin’s.

outcomes.remark: ‘as justiças’: just acts (heard first) / forms of justice or judgement
outcomes.reason: The plural was heard as the draft meant it; kept.

outcomes.remark: ‘o seu rosto’: the Lord’s (heard first) / the just man’s
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: aljava
outcomes.reason: The one word for a quiver; the image is the Latin’s.

outcomes.remark: unknown words: ímpio, iniquidade
outcomes.reason: Glossary words (ímpius → ímpio, iníquitas → iniquidade), listed as unknown in earlier psalms too.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: equidade
outcomes.reason: Glossary (ǽquitas → equidade; also listed as unknown in Ps 118).

audit.note: v2. Three changes against draft 1: 10:2 ‘como dizeis vós’ (the subject named, after the blind reader heard ‘dizeis’ as said to the Lord); 10:5b ‘estão voltados para’ (the stylist’s, for ‘olham para’); 10:7 the commas of the list removed (the stylist’s). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the three v1 critics read).
Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags as draft 1 (10:2 +3, 10:3 +4, 10:7 +4), accepted for the same reasons; ‘como dizeis vós’ adds a syllable to a colon that was two short of the Latin’s.

Draft 2 — the gate: clean. ‘A tradução conserva o conteúdo, as imagens e as particularidades do latim em todos os versículos, sem falhas de adequação identificadas. As marcas de divisão são as mesmas e aparecem na mesma ordem que no original.’ So ‘como dizeis vós’ (the subject named) and ‘estão voltados para’ (a participle of state for respíciunt) passed.

Draft 2, Portuguese only — run to test the one fault of draft 1. 10:2 ‘como dizeis vós’ is now heard first as said to other people (‘sem ficar claro quem são’ — nor does the Latin say); the fault is mended. Seventeen items; the same four unknown words. New in this reading, none a fault: 10:5a ‘templo santo’ heard as an earthly temple until ‘no céu’ corrects it (the Latin’s own movement); 10:7 ‘laços’ heard as rope loops falling from the sky ‘sem necessariamente reconhecer o sentido de armadilhas’ (draft 1’s reader heard snares first; láqueus → laço is the glossary’s, Ps 90:3); 10:8 ‘as justiças’ heard this time as the quality before the acts — neither reading is the courts, which was the risk.

outcomes.remark: ‘como dizeis vós’: other people (heard first) / the Lord
outcomes.reason: The fix of draft 2 works: heard as said to others.

outcomes.remark: ‘o que aperfeiçoastes’: the Lord (heard first) / the addressees of 10:2; the change of addressee not explicit
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; the Latin marks the change only by number, which Portuguese vós cannot.

outcomes.remark: ‘no seu templo santo’: an earthly temple (heard first) / a heavenly dwelling
outcomes.reason: The Latin is as open, and its second colon moves to heaven as the Portuguese does.

outcomes.remark: ‘o pobre’: without means (heard first) / afflicted
outcomes.reason: pauper is as wide.

outcomes.remark: ‘laços’: snares / knots / bonds; heard as rope loops, not necessarily snares
outcomes.reason: láqueus → laço (glossary); a noose is a snare; draft 1’s reader heard ‘armadilhas’ first. ‘armadilhas’ would explain the image.

outcomes.remark: ‘as justiças’: just acts / justice as a quality (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Neither reading is wrong; the plural is the Latin’s.

outcomes.remark: ‘o seu rosto viu a equidade’: witnessed / looked with approval on
outcomes.reason: Both are in vidit.
